q8.answer: Counts live in one shared Redis instance (primary plus replica), under the key rl:{customerId}:{windowStart}, so all 6 gateways see the same number. Old counts are removed by a 120 s expiry set by the Lua script when the count first reaches 1.

q9.answer: Budget resets when a new clock minute starts, because the key includes the window start and a new window uses a new key with count 0. It is a fixed window, not sliding; the old key just expires after 120 s. A denied request does not use budget.

q10.answer: The check and increment run in a single Lua script on Redis, which executes as one uninterrupted step. So two gateways cannot both read count below limit and both take the last slot; the second one sees the updated count and gets DENIED.

q11.answer: Retry-After is windowStart + 60 - now, computed inside the Lua script using Redis TIME (never gateway clocks), rounded up to whole seconds with a minimum of 1, sent as a plain integer on the 429.

q12.answer: No retry: the gateway fails open on an error or no reply within 50 ms, forwards the request, and emits the ratelimit_store_unavailable metric. The client gets no X-RateLimit-Limit or X-RateLimit-Remaining headers, since the remaining count is unknown.
